quest.title: To Yesterday
quest.description: One day, you and Paimon arrive at the Adventurers' Guild to check out the commissions there...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to the Court of Fontaine's Adventurers' Guild

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Katheryne, it's us! Got any new commissions? Specifically, one with a huge Mora tag, perhaps...?

choices.text: You didn't have to be so direct...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, Paimon's just being enthusiastic. We're old friends now, she gets it!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hehe, it's always a pleasure to see our two most avid adventurers again. Looking for the next challenge, I see.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Actually, we do in fact have a rather urgent commission that is still open. Having read the details, however, I don't believe you'd consider it to be "lucrative"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, don't worry about that. We were just kidding. So what's the situation?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: To put it simply, the requester is looking for a temporary replacement actress for their musical. The original cast member ran into some issues, and is currently unable to perform the role.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: But the troupe has also been experiencing some financial difficulties, so unfortunately they cannot afford to pay the replacement actress...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... That does sound like a tricky situation. So basically, they're looking for a volunteer?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: That's right. Our adventurers reached out to many actresses, but none of them were willing to take the job.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: There are only a few days left until the performance. If they can't find someone in time, they'll probably have to postpone the show. And delays tend to create all sorts of new problems...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Got it... Oh... This one's a doozy. What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Any ideas?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if we took the commission, neither of us have any experience starring in musicals...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Very true...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hmm... If you're interested in helping, why not start by having a chat with the requester? He's right over there.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Maybe you can't fill the role yourselves, but you might be able to help him figure out another solution. Maybe there's something he hasn't thought of.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, it's that guy, huh? No wonder he looks like he just ate a sour lemon.

choices.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon approves. Let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hello there! Are you the guy looking for a new actress?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Wait... I know you two! Are you really willing to act in my musical!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, sounds like we're pretty famous in Fontaine already! Heehee.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... But to answer your question, neither of us have any experience in musicals... But we heard that you're in a bit of a bind, so we figured we could at least try to help you think of a solution.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Ah, I see... It's okay, I knew that asking for a volunteer was a long shot.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: If we can't find someone to step in, we'll have no choice but to cancel the show... It would be such a shame.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can't you cover the budget for a new actress with ticket fees?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: *sigh* That's the thing... We're not some high-profile theater troupe. Just a group of amateur enthusiasts.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: All our sets and props are very crude. We're grateful enough just to get an audience, never mind ticket fees.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: If we had a way to make this profitable, things might've turned out differently... But now it looks inevitable that we'll disband.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Disband? You're splitting up the troupe?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Oh, I guess the lady at the Adventurers' Guild didn't tell you? Yeah... This is supposed to be our final show together as a troupe.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: One last show, and after that, we go our separate ways. So we were really hoping to end on a high note.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Nobody wants things to just... fizzle out. Not after all the time and effort we've invested into it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Katheryne mentioned that one of your actresses can't make it?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Yeah... the leading lady, in fact. She's been dealing with a chronic illness ever since childhood, and unfortunately it flared up again recently. It really drains all her energy, so she's in no state to perform.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: The show just won't be the same without her... But for everyone else's sake, I still hope we can find a way to hold the performance on schedule.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it. We have a clearer picture now... Um... Let's see if we can come up with any ideas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... What if we sponsored the show? Um... Traveler, how much Mora are you carrying?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Ah, please, there's no need to go that far. I wouldn't feel right asking such a huge favor, and I can't promise that we'd ever be able to pay you back.

choices.text: Mora isn't the biggest problem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, good point. If the actress just goes through the motions for the Mora, that's not exactly rescuing the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should find someone who'll put on the best performance possible. Hmm... Ooh, wait! What about you-know-who...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Great minds think alike. I was just thinking that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, that's how you know we're the best of partners! Anyway, she should have all the free time in the world right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's really good at performing, and she was once super popular with the crowd... performing in a musical should be a piece of cake for her!

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Who are you thinking of? Sounds like someone famous...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Furina.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Her!? You're... That was a joke, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Nope. Paimon doesn't actually know if she's performed on stage before, but Paimon's pretty confident that she'd be really good at it.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: You're not wrong there... She has actually performed in a number of big-name shows before. They were one of the reasons she was so popular...

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: But even if she's no longer the Hydro Archon, it's not like she's suddenly a commoner.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: She's still an idol to many people in Fontaine, including myself... I just think Lady Furina might feel a bit out of place in an amateur troupe like ours.

choices.text: You want the show to go ahead, don't you?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Well yes, but... but...

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Huh... Fair enough, I mean, if she was actually willing to, then of course I'd be honored to have Lady Furina star in our show. I'm sure the rest of the troupe would be delighted too.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: I'm sure everyone in our troupe has probably dreamt of performing on stage with her one day.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Of course, it all depends on whether she's interested... She might consider this opportunity beneath her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No point stressing about that. We'll only know if we ask her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And besides, things are different now. There's no reason for her to be all high and mighty anymore.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go. It'll be good to check in on her anyway.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Thank you for your help... I guess I'll just stay here and wait for the good news. Good luck!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait, where does Furina actually live nowadays? She used to live in luxury at the Palais Mermonia, but she's, uh... moved out, right?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: As it happens, I have her current address here. I can provide it to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, when did you get here!?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hehe, I came over when things were starting to sound more promising. I thought I should be at the ready in case my assistance is needed.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It is my duty to support commissioners in any way I can.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Thank you, Ma'am... Thank you so much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, now that we've got the address, we'll go find Furina. Back in a jiffy!

choices.text: Are you prepared to do whatever it takes?
How do we find someone who's a good fit for the role?
We'll go talk to him.
The more lucrative, the better!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know we're worth it! For quality work and speedy results, choose the Paimon and the Traveler!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Did Katheryne really give us the right address? She lives... here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—Not that there's anything wrong with this place, it's just, uh... a bit of a step down from the Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You know, it's common courtesy to make sure the homeowner isn't in earshot when you're denigrating their abode.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Okay, when did popping out of thin air become all the rage!? First Katheryne, and now you...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I was just out on a shopping trip. I ran out of macaroni, so I went to grab a few more bags.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I used to have a much wider range of choices when it came to food, but now, I'm finding that simple, traditional home cooking can be quite delicious too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Don't you get sick of macaroni every day?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Not at all. As long as you have different kinds of sauces in, you can have macaroni and tomato sauce one week, macaroni and bolognese the next...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, sounds like you're really struggling to cope...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it because you have to do all your own cooking now?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: How rude! Questioning my cooking skills, the audacity!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's not like I have a very eventful life these days. Actually, I barely leave the house. So I don't see how it's unusual that my meals are a little simpler now too.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Besides, I'm sure I could master dishes like "La Lettre a Focalors" or "Blubber Profiteroles" in no time. If I felt so inclined.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, there it is. You don't know how to cook!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Pff, not yet, maybe, but... Anyway! What are you even doing here? I do hope you didn't come here just to ogle at my fall from grace?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Let me first be clear that I'm not taking guests at this time. So if you're just here to clown around, then please be on your way! Shoo!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, we're sorry! Please don't be mad!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon was just showing concern for your wellbeing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, exactly. What {NICKNAME} said! Paimon wasn't trying to make fun of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Hang on a sec, you weren't exactly holding back either!

choices.text: That's not important.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: My help, hmm? Well, maybe you're forgetting that I'm no longer the mighty Hydro Archon. I don't even have a Vision, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, it's nothing that serious! It's just very specific, and you're the one with the power to help.

choices.text: If not you, then no one.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh? Well, if that's the case, then... fine, I'll spare you the lecture about your attitude just now.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: So tell me. What, specifically, makes this matter so... specific?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Furina about the troupe's plans for its final performance.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah, I see... I knew you couldn't have come all this way just to amuse yourselves at my expense.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: After all, I was once the brightest star in all of Fontaine, well-versed in all the various performing arts. A mere musical is well within my capabilities...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...But given the present circumstances, I'm afraid I must regretfully decline your casting request.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How come? It sounds like this'd be a breeze for you.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: True, but I have made a decision to retire from the stage.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Although I am no longer required to play the role of the Hydro Archon, the time I spent inhabiting that character has left an indelible mark on me.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Centuries of pretending to be a different person changes you completely. I'm not the same person I once was.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Of course, that can't be undone now. It's too late, and I have no intention of reinventing myself all over again.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But at least I can say that I no longer desire to play any new roles.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So that's how you really feel...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can understand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But this is just a one-off part to fill in for someone who's sick. Surely that's okay?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Whether it's a one-off or not, it's a boundary that I've committed to no longer cross.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If I make an exception to the rule now, I'm just leaving a backdoor for myself. Which would be the same as not having a boundary in the first place.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: So I'm not going to perform, and that is that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, guess there's no convincing you... Well, is there anything else we can do to help out the troupe? Otherwise, they'll just have to disband without any fanfare...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you know any other actors who might be interested in the role?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Nope.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Short and to the point, okay...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I've never been great at maintaining relationships. Besides, anyone I've ever worked with probably couldn't wait to get rid of me...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Since I'm just an ordinary person now. They'll probably just laugh in my face if I go asking them for help...

choices.text: You shouldn't assume the worst of people.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: True, but.. I mean, could you even blame them? I show up out of the blue, begging and groveling for their help with a show they won't even get paid for? ...*shudders* No way, I'm dying from embarassment just thinking about it. Nope, not happening!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Is there anything else we can do? This performance really means a lot to the guy we're working for...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Have I not made myself clear? You're barking up the wrong tree. I don't want this job, nor do I know of anyone else who would.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...Sorry, I didn't mean for that to sound so harsh. I wish I could help, really. But if I thought I had the answer to this problem, I would've said so by now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's alright, Furina. Paimon just wanted to make sure we tried everything. *sigh* Everyone in the troupe will be so disappointed...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's try to come up with a plan B.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, guess that's all we can do now. Alright then, we'll see you around, Furina...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Toodle-oo to you too. I'm going home to take a rest now.

choices.text: What's wrong with making one exception?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Look, I'm sorry, okay!? I'm sorry I drew a line in the sand without thinking about every possible grain on the other side!

choices.text: You're the only person for the job.
We actually came here to ask you for your help...

talks.objective: Go back and pass on the word about Furina's views

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on? Are they arguing?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: ...That's besides the point. I'll ask you again. Why did you start looking for a replacement without my consent? When did I tell you I'm going to take a step back?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: You didn't need to say it... We've known each other for how long now? We know the signs. But you never tell us about your illness even when it's clearly flaring up.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: And that gives you the right to make a decision on my behalf?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Shortly after you left, the troupe's lead actress came to the Adventurers' Guild. She believes that she's healthy enough to perform.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Excuse me, but can you both take a moment to discuss something else for now? The adventurer assigned to your commission has returned.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Sorry, I was just dealing with a little misunderstanding. So, how did your conversation with Furina go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sadly, it's a no from her. We tried to persuade her, but she wasn't having it. She doesn't want to play the role, for personal reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: I see... Well, circumstances have changed a little, so maybe that's not such bad news after all.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: You see, our leading lady has just informed me that she's well enough to make it to the show after all. Staging the musical with the full original cast was always the dream, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... Sounds like everything worked itself out then.

choices.text: Imagine if we had managed to convince Furina to join...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, she'd be livid! We'd get the scolding of a lifetime!

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Geez... Is Lady Furina really so harsh with people?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Only joking, calm down! ...So, uh, guess we can consider this case closed now, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Despite the fact that we failed to complete the commission... We were still racking our brains for ideas on the way back here, hehe.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: *sigh* Look, there's no point arguing with you about this any more. You've made yourself very clear, so I'll stop looking for a replacement.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: This is the last chance we have, though. If your illness flares up again, there won't be time to find anyone to replace you.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: So, are you absolutely sure you'll be able to handle it? The whole team is putting everything they have into this final performance. We have to make sure it goes ahead.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Yes, I'm completely confident. I've been taking a new medication from the doctor, and it's working brilliantly. I'll definitely be able to tough it out until the performance day.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: I share everyone's desire to commemorate all our years as a troupe with a proper farewell show. So the last thing I want is to be left out.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Every one of us thinks of this troupe as their home. Myself included.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: You're right. I'm sorry — I let myself get too worried about the show. I should have asked for your permission first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, all's well that ends well! Sounds like the show will go on.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, wait here a second.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Sure.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hey, how did you... I—I was just passing by because... I realized I forgot a couple of items on my shopping list!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...Alright, alright, I'm coming. No need to drag me!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Uh... Ahem, hello one and all. I couldn't help but overhear your conversation just now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Furina!? Didn't you say you were gonna take a rest at home? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I... I was just ever so slightly concerned about the situation you mentioned. Yes. A teensy bit concerned, that's all.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: When you came to talk with me earlier, I jumped right to explaining my position, and said some strongly worded things.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And all before I even had a full grasp of the situation... Anyway, I just feel a bit bad about how it went down.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm sorry, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's totally fine! Paimon didn't take any of that personally!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then why didn't you just show yourself?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...You really have a knack for asking the most uncomfortable questions, don't you...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I felt very sheepish, having had a change of heart after flatly refusing you. And then, to make matters worse, you caught me...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But in any case, it sounds like the issue has already been resolved?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Yeah... When they said they were gonna ask for your help, I almost had a heart attack. I mean, how could we be worthy of having Lady Furina star in our show?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: There's no need to think like that, and no need to keep addressing me as "Lady." Just "Furina" is fine.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I was wondering... if this troupe is so important to all of you, why does it have to disband?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If the difficulties are purely financial, then there must be a solution. You could put the shows on pause while you look for a sponsor, for instance.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Everyone seems so devoted to the troupe. I'm sure if you keep chipping away, you'll find a way through.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: *sigh* We all want to believe that, but... Some things are just beyond our control.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: ...Everything's been going downhill ever since we lost our director. She was the heart and soul of our troupe. She kept us going.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Her name was Aurelie, and she was the founder as well as the artistic director of our troupe. And tragically, she... was a victim in the serial disappearances case.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: That's actually how I recognized these two. It was all thanks to their efforts that the true culprit was brought to justice.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: *sigh* But still... No sentence can bring our director back to us.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: She was a loyal fan of your performances, Lady— Uh, Miss Furina. They were what first inspired her to get into musical theater.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: She rallied many people around her who were destitute or had lost their sense of purpose in life, and convinced them to join her troupe. She wrote her own scripts, acted on stage, and mentored each and every one of us.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: People loved our performances back then... We seemed to be going from strength to strength. Things were really looking up for us...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And then, disaster struck...

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Yeah. After that, the entire troupe fell into disarray.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: None of us know anything about scriptwriting, let alone how to handle the business side of things. We've been doing the best we can, but despite our efforts, things are slowly but surely falling apart.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: It's agonizing, but ultimately, we'd rather end things now on our own terms than stick it out to the bitter end and watch all our dreams turn to dust.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's so sad...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What a terrible waste... A gifted artist from humble beginnings, who achieved so much and no doubt had much more to give... and then her life was so cruelly taken.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I suppose it's fair to say, then, that this final show, besides being your farewell to the stage, is also your final gift for her?

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Yes, exactly. We all miss her terribly.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, good thing I followed the Traveler here. After hearing this tragic tale, I can no longer stand by and do nothing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Furina?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I know what you're thinking, but I by no means plan to cross the boundary I've set for myself. Besides, they're no longer looking for a replacement anyway.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I can, however, provide some artistic guidance from the vantage point of a highly experienced audience member.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But only if you feel this is something that would help, of course.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Oh, most definitely! We'll take any guidance that you can give!

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: We unfortunately don't have any budget for a consultant, though... Will that be a problem?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I don't need any compensation. All I'd ask in return, if you're willing, is that you tell me some more about the life and work of your late director.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Something I've begun to realize since my departure from the Opera Epiclese is that there's a lot you don't see when you observe everything from on high.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: The law only judges criminal behavior, and does not weigh human emotion. The court's verdict can settle the question of criminal liability, but...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What about all the unresolved emotions of the parties involved? What happens to them?

choices.text: A verdict can bring emotional catharsis.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: An interesting answer. But if you ask me, I think all emotion shall ultimately return home to the heart, and slowly settle with the passage of time.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Take, par exemple, how this troupe pines for their late director... Things such as this I have never witnessed before. And so, I should like to observe, perchance to understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Still a fan of your old dramatic monologues then, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You just wanna get back in on the action, don't you?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: No, no, no, this is a completely different situation! Hmph, pearls before swine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The name's not "Swine," it's Paimon!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Would you be willing to join me? C'mon, take a break from adventuring to listen to a story.

choices.text: Since it's you, I'll do it.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Thank you all so much. Our director was a huge fan of Miss Furina's performances... as, of course, we all are.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Alright, follow me. We'll go to our usual practice space. Please excuse the size — it's a little on the smaller side.

choices.text: Especially since it's related to the serial disappearances case.
They come pouring out, and flow away into infinity.
...Only for her to find out she's no longer needed.

dialogues.speaker: Buraud
dialogues.text: Huh? L—Lady Furina!?

dialogues.speaker: Elain
dialogues.text: What's Lady Furina doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Hello, all. Allow me to explain. As of today, La— Uh, Miss Furina will be supporting our production of "The Little Oceanid" in the role of artistic consultant.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: These two over here are the ones that made it possible — they kindly reached out to Miss Furina on our behalf. I'm sure they need no introduction.

dialogues.speaker: Buraud
dialogues.text: You bet! That was the trial of the century!

dialogues.speaker: Elain
dialogues.text: You helped bring our director's murderer to justice. We can't thank you enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, please don't mention it. We're just here to join in on the fun.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So, you were saying — "The Little Oceanid"...?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's the name of our final show. It's an unfinished script left behind by our director.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: One of our greatest regrets is that she never got to complete it. So if we can bring it to the stage and make it a successful show, we can all take some solace in that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but if it's not finished, then...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Finding an actress was the least of your problems...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Yeah, we've been battling issues on every front trying to realize this dream... Anyway, let me give you a quick summary of what the story's all about.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: The protagonist of the story is a young Oceanid who transforms herself into human form, despite the protests of her family.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: She longed to live just like any other human. And sure enough, she found friendship and even love. Everything seemed perfect.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: But one day, her true identity was exposed, and her world came crashing down around her...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So far, so good. A classic tale. What happened after that?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: That's one of the issues we've been trying to deal with... Unfortunately, this was as far as the director got with her script.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: We need a proper ending so we can bring this musical to the stage, but people have different opinions on which direction to take it in.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: We still haven't decided between a happy ending or a true-to-life tragedy.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: By true-to-life, you mean... the director's sudden disappearance?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Yeah. Like they say, truth is stranger than fiction.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: But then there's the question of whether we really want to use the stage to pass our raw pain onto the audience.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Exactly. A lot of the time, people come to watch a show just hoping for some light entertainment. We have to consider their emotional stake in this, not just our own.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: And one last thing — we're still waiting on confirmation from two of our main actors.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: The first is Pauleau, who plays the protagonist's lover. He's locked himself away to focus on writing an ending for the script. But the deadline's past and we still haven't heard from him.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: The other is Vilmant, who plays the main antagonist. He took the director's death pretty hard. Hasn't set foot in the city since.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: He did write to us, promising that he'll be there for the final performance, but we haven't seen or heard from him since. So we're not really sure what to make of that.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Although... Now that we have Miss Furina helping us, maybe we should take the opportunity to get everyone back together?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What opportunity? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Hehe, maybe you're unaware, but your name has always been like a rallying cry for us.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Our director was constantly singing your praises. All of us look up to you as a role model.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh stop, you're making me all flustered. Although... hehe, not in a bad way.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I suspect the reason they're dragging their feet is that they have their doubts about whether the show will really go ahead, considering all the issues you've been facing.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But one by one, all the obstacles are being removed. Now is the time to rally the troops.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Makes sense... Okay, priority number one — let's check in with Pauleau and see where he's at with the ending.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: He went back to Poisson a few days ago. Said that staying in a friend's home might help him to relax and escape the feeling of isolation.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: I thought the last thing his friend would want right now would be to take visitors, given that Poisson was flooded not too long ago. But I guess it's the opposite — a friend in need and all that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, maybe he could use some company.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Poisson...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Nothing... I suppose my presence will be indispensable if we are to restore his faith in the show.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So, allons-y! To Poisson!

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: I can't believe they're seriously asking Lady Furina. Seems a little over the top...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Try not to worry. May I pour you a glass of water?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's too bad, but we have to respect Furina's decision.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe the thought of performing brings up too many painful memories now...
